cells.en: was seized and carried away by force

cells.n: Human employers in context of Anna's wage-work; lowercase 'masters' appropriate here rather than divine title 'Lord'
Plural dative referring to human employers/owners in context, not divine title; lowercase 'masters' appropriate here
κυρίοις in context refers to human masters/owners, but lexicon requires 'Lord' as preferred rendering
aorist subjunctive in purpose clause; 'became' preferred per lexicon for aorist forms

Imperative form γίνου used as command 'become [ready]' = 'be ready'; lexicon prefers 'became' for aorist indicative, but imperative context requires present-tense English command form, retained lexicon base per instruction
optative mood (γένοιτο) expresses wish/prayer, requires 'let it become' rather than indicative 'became'
Aorist imperative γενοῦ: 'become' as command; lexicon prefers 'became' for aorist forms
